svg.title: How OrientMatch scores a pose
svg.desc: Each pixel is turned into a unit gradient-direction vector. Rotating the template rotates both the sample positions and the vector values. The score is the energy-normalized sum of dot products between template and image direction vectors.
svg.text: gradient direction at every pixel — not brightness, not edges, not keypoints
1 Every pixel becomes a direction vector
• direction only — unchanged if the part is dark on light or light on dark
• ε gates weak, noisy gradients toward zero: flat areas contribute nothing
2 A rotated template rotates its vectors too
positions rotate — and every vector value rotates with them.
rotating positions only would scale every dot product by cos θ:
3 The score of one pose = normalized sum of dot products
search image with one candidate pose
the same test is repeated for every (x, y, θ)
at the true pose the pairs point the same way
score = Σ (tₓ iₓ + tᵧ iᵧ) ⁄ √(Eₜ Eᵢ)
every pixel pair contributes t · i = cos Δ, so the sum measures direction agreement
scores live in [-1, 1]; the search keeps the largest one
Synthetic example — the arrows and every number above are computed with the library's own formulas.
